subject: general
question:
Fill in the blank:
The National Air Quality Index (AQI) is measured using ______ number of pollutants.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eight**__.

**__Key Points__**

• The **National Air Quality Index (AQI)** was launched by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** in **September 2014** in **New Delhi**. It was introduced as part of the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** to provide a simplified tool for the common man to understand the air quality in their vicinity.

• The **AQI** is calculated based on **eight** major air pollutants for which **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)** have been prescribed. These **eight** pollutants are **Particulate Matter (PM10)**, **Particulate Matter (PM2.5)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)**, **Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Ozone (O3)**, **Ammonia (NH3)**, and **Lead (Pb)**.

• The index was developed by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in consultation with **IIT Kanpur** and other medical and air quality professionals. It follows the **One Number-One Color-One Description** mantra to communicate the health impacts of air pollution effectively.
